questions.question: When the same current flows through two wires of equal length but different resistances, the wire with higher resistance will:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Produce more heat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Joule’s Law of Heating**, the heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to the **resistance** of the conductor when the **current** and **time** of flow are constant.
 
• The mathematical expression for heat generated is **H = I²Rt**, where **H** is the heat produced, **I** is the **electric current**, **R** is the **electrical resistance**, and **t** is the **time duration** for which the current flows.
 
• In the given scenario, the **current (I)** and **length** (which implies similar conditions for time or setup) are equal for both wires. Since **H ∝ R**, the wire with the **higher resistance** will generate a greater amount of **thermal energy**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Produce more heat.***
 
• Statement A suggests the wires produce the same heat; this is incorrect because heat production depends on **resistance**, and the resistances are stated to be different. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• Statement B suggests no heat is produced; this is impossible as whenever **current** flows through a **resistor**, energy is dissipated as heat due to collisions between **electrons** and **atoms**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• Statement D suggests the wire with higher resistance produces less heat; this contradicts **Joule's Law** where **H** is **directly proportional** to **R**. ***Hence, statement D is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:** The **resistance (R)** of a wire depends on its **length (L)**, **cross-sectional area (A)**, and the **resistivity (ρ)** of the material, represented by the formula **R = ρ(L/A)**. Even if lengths are equal, differences in **material** or **thickness** result in different resistances.
 
• **Applications of Heating Effect:** The **heating effect of electric current** is utilized in various household appliances such as **electric irons**, **electric heaters**, **geysers**, and **toasters**. These devices use **heating elements** made of materials with **high resistivity** and **high melting points**, such as **Nichrome** (an alloy of **Nickel** and **Chromium**).
 
• **Electric Fuse:** A **safety device** called an **electric fuse** works on the heating effect of current. It consists of a wire with a **low melting point**; when **excessive current** flows, the heat produced (**I²Rt**) melts the fuse wire, breaking the **circuit** to prevent **fire** or **damage**.
 
• **Energy Conversion:** This phenomenon represents the conversion of **electrical energy** into **heat energy**. The standard **SI unit** of heat is the **Joule (J)**, but it is often measured in **calories** (**1 calorie = 4.184 Joules**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Series vs Parallel Circuits:** In a **series circuit**, the **current (I)** is the same through all components, so the component with **higher resistance** produces **more heat**. However, in a **parallel circuit**, the **voltage (V)** is the same, and heat is calculated using **H = (V²/R)t**, meaning the **lower resistance** wire would produce **more heat**.
 
• **Tungsten in Bulbs:** The **filament** of an **incandescent light bulb** is made of **Tungsten** because of its **high resistance** and an extremely high **melting point** of approximately **3422°C**, allowing it to glow and emit light without melting.
 
• **Power Dissipation:** The rate at which heat is produced is called **Electric Power (P)**. It is measured in **Watts (W)** and calculated as **P = I²R** or **P = VI**. In **1841**, **James Prescott Joule** first quantified this relationship, which is why it bears his name.

questions.question: Which of the following terms is used to describe the ability of a plant to recover its lost parts by growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regeneration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Regeneration** is defined as the biological process by which an organism replaces or restores **lost or damaged cells**, tissues, organs, and even entire body parts to full functionality. ***Hence, option A is correct.***
 
• In the plant kingdom, this ability is highly developed due to **totipotency**, a unique characteristic where a single plant cell has the genetic potential to divide and produce all the differentiated cells of the **entire organism**.
 
• This process often involves the formation of a **callus**, which is an unorganized mass of **parenchyma cells**. These cells eventually undergo **differentiation** to form new roots, stems, or leaves.
 
• **Regeneration** serves as a vital survival strategy for plants, allowing them to recover from **herbivory**, environmental damage, or physical **fragmentation**.
 
• It is distinctly different from regular growth, as it specifically refers to the **repair or replacement** of structures that were previously present but subsequently removed or destroyed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fertilisation**:

 
 
• This is the process of the fusion of **male gametes** (sperm/pollen) with **female gametes** (egg/ovule) to form a **diploid zygote**.
 
• It is the fundamental step in **sexual reproduction**, ensuring genetic diversity through the combination of DNA from **two** parents.
 
• It does not involve the recovery of lost somatic parts but rather the **creation** of a new generation. ***Hence, option B is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Budding**:
 
 
• A form of **asexual reproduction** where a new individual develops from a small anatomical projection or **bud** on the parent organism.
 
• Commonly observed in organisms like **Yeast** and **Hydra**. In plants, this is utilized in **horticulture** as a method of **grafting**.
 
• While it involves growth, it is a reproductive mechanism to produce **offspring** rather than a repair mechanism for the parent. ***Hence, option C is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission**:
 
 
• A primary method of **asexual reproduction** in **prokaryotic** organisms like **bacteria** and certain **protozoa** such as **Amoeba**.
 
• The parent cell divides into **two** approximately equal-sized daughter cells, each receiving a copy of the **genetic material**.
 
• This process is related to **population increase** in **single-celled** organisms and not the regrowth of specialized organs in multicellular plants. ***Hence, option D is incorrect.***

__
 
• The letter **‘G’** in the term **G20** stands for **Group**. Therefore, **G20** refers to the **Group of Twenty**, which is a premier forum for international economic cooperation.
 
• The **G20** is composed of **19 sovereign countries**, the **European Union (EU)**, and the **African Union (AU)**. It plays a critical role in shaping and strengthening global architecture and governance on all major international economic issues.
 
• The **Digital Economy Working Group (DEWG)** is one of the specialized tracks under the **Sherpa Track** of the **G20**. The second meeting of this group in **2025** was hosted by **South Africa**, focusing on **digital public infrastructure**, **artificial intelligence**, and **digital inclusion**.
 
• **South Africa** officially assumed the **G20 Presidency** on **December 1, 2024**, succeeding **Brazil**. It is the first **African nation** to hold the presidency of this elite **Group**.
 
• The **G20** members represent around **85%** of the **global GDP**, over **75%** of the **global trade**, and about **two-thirds** of the **world population**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Evolution**: The **G20** was founded in **1999** after the **Asian financial crisis** as a forum for **Finance Ministers** and **Central Bank Governors** to discuss global economic and financial issues. It was upgraded to the level of **Heads of State/Government** in the wake of the **2008 global financial crisis**.
 
• **Member Countries**: The members include **Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Republic of Korea, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Türkiye, the United Kingdom, and the United States**.
 
• **The African Union (AU)**: In a historic move during the **18th G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi, India**, in **September 2023**, the **African Union** was admitted as a permanent member of the **Group**, significantly enhancing the representation of **developing economies**.
 
• **Working Structure**: The **G20** operates through two parallel tracks: the **Finance Track** and the **Sherpa Track**. The **Sherpa Track** focuses on non-financial issues such as **agriculture, culture, digital economy, and health**, while the **Finance Track** is led by **Finance Ministers** and **Central Bank Governors**.
 
• **Presidency and Troika**: The **G20 Presidency** rotates annually. The **Troika** consists of the **previous, current, and incoming presidencies** to ensure continuity. For the year **2025**, the **Troika** included **Brazil, South Africa, and the United States**.

• **Location and Dates**: The second **Digital Economy Working Group** meeting took place in **South Africa** during the first half of **2025**, serving as a preparatory step for the final **Leaders' Summit** held in **Johannesburg/Pretoria**.
 
• **Functions of DEWG**: The **Digital Economy Working Group** (formerly the Digital Economy Task Force) was established in **2017** under the **German Presidency** to address the challenges and opportunities of **digitalization** for economic growth.

questions.question: Which of the following initiative by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) specifically announced that India’s 'common compute capacity' has crossed 34,000 GPUs to boost indigenous AI foundation-model development?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IndiaAI Mission** was approved by the **Union Cabinet** in **March 2024** with a comprehensive financial outlay of **₹10,371.92 crore**. This mission is a landmark initiative designed to catalyze **India’s** **AI** ecosystem by providing critical infrastructure and support for innovation.
 
• One of the primary pillars of this mission is the **IndiaAI Compute Capacity**, which aims to establish a high-end **GPU** (Graphics Processing Unit) based compute infrastructure. The **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** recently highlighted that the 'common compute capacity' in **India** has crossed the threshold of **34,000 GPUs**, which is a significant milestone for **indigenous AI foundation-model** development.
 
• The mission operates on a **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)** model. It seeks to provide **AI** startups, researchers, and government agencies with subsidized access to high-performance computing resources, reducing the cost of training large **AI** models.
 
• The initiative is aimed at building **Sovereign AI** capabilities for **India**. This ensures that the nation has control over its data and the underlying technology used for critical sectors like **healthcare**, **agriculture**, and **governance**.
 
• Under the **IndiaAI Mission**, the government intends to procure or facilitate the availability of at least **10,000 GPUs** specifically for the public segment, while the broader ecosystem (including private players) is expected to scale significantly beyond that, as reflected in the **34,000 GPUs** milestone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Components of IndiaAI Mission:**

 
 
• **IndiaAI Innovation Centre:** This focuses on the development and deployment of indigenous **Large Multimodal Models (LMMs)** and domain-specific foundational models.
 
• **IndiaAI Datasets Platform:** It aims to streamline access to non-personal **data** for **India**-based **AI** researchers and startups, ensuring high-quality data is available for model training.
 
• **IndiaAI FutureSkills:** This component focuses on human capital by increasing **AI** literacy and advanced skills among the youth, targeting the creation of a specialized workforce in the **AI** domain.
 
 
 
• **Sovereign AI and GPU Significance:**
 
 
• **Sovereign AI** refers to a **country's** ability to produce **AI** using its own **infrastructure**, **data**, **workforce**, and **business networks**.
 
• **GPUs** are specialized electronic circuits designed to accelerate the creation of images and are now the gold standard for processing **AI** algorithms due to their parallel processing capabilities. questions.question: As reported by Feeding India (an NGO) in June 2025, the big fat Indian wedding is quietly triggering a climate chaos by adding which of the following gases in the atmosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the report released by **Feeding India** in **June 2025**, the "big fat Indian wedding" industry is a significant contributor to environmental degradation through massive food waste. When large quantities of unconsumed food are discarded, they eventually reach **landfills**.
 
• In these **landfills**, the food waste undergoes **anaerobic decomposition** (breaking down without oxygen), which leads to the significant emission of **Methane** (CH4). This gas is a highly potent **greenhouse gas** that traps heat in the atmosphere. ***Hence, the statement regarding Methane is correct.***
 
• The data suggests that approximately **10% to 20%** of the food prepared for large weddings in **India** goes to waste. This translates to thousands of tonnes of organic waste being generated during the peak wedding **months** of **November**, **December**, and **January**.
 
• **Feeding India**, a non-profit organization initiated by **Zomato**, highlighted that this "climate chaos" is often overlooked compared to industrial emissions, yet the **Methane** released from such events significantly accelerates **global warming**.
 
• The report emphasizes that **Methane** has a **Global Warming Potential** (GWP) that is significantly higher than **Carbon Dioxide** over a short-term period, making wedding waste a critical climate issue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Feeding India:**

 
 
• It was founded in **2014** and later became a part of **Zomato** to tackle the dual problem of hunger and food waste in **India**.
 
• The organization operates in over **100 cities** and utilizes a network of **volunteers** to collect surplus food from weddings and corporate events to feed the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Methane (CH4):**
 
 
• **Methane** is a colorless, odorless gas and is the primary component of **natural gas**.
 
• It is **25 to 28 times** more effective at trapping heat than **Carbon Dioxide** (CO2) over a **100-year** period, according to the **Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)**.
 
• Major sources include **agriculture** (enteric fermentation in livestock), **landfills**, and **fossil fuel** extraction.
 
 
 
• **Waste Management Rules in India:**
 
 
• The **Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016** mandate the segregation of waste at source into dry, wet, and hazardous categories.
 
• Under these rules, bulk waste generators like **wedding halls** and **hotels** are responsible for processing their biodegradable waste on-site through **composting** or **biomethanation**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Other Gases:**
 
 
• **Nitrous Oxide (N2O):** Primarily released from **agricultural** soil management and synthetic **fertilizers**; it is **300 times** more potent than CO2.
 
• **Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs):** Used in **air conditioning** and **refrigeration** systems often found in wedding venues; they have a very high **global warming potential**.
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO):** A byproduct of incomplete combustion, often found in **vehicular emissions** around crowded event locations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scale of the Problem:** **India** hosts approximately **10 million** weddings every **year**. The cumulative impact of food waste from these events creates a substantial ecological footprint.
 
• **Global Commitments:** **India** is a signatory to various international climate agreements. Managing **short-lived climate pollutants** like **Methane** is crucial for meeting the targets set under the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• **Technological Solutions:** The use of **Bio-digesters** in large venues can convert organic waste into **biogas**, which can be used as a clean **fuel**, thereby preventing the release of **Methane** into the **atmosphere**.
 
• **Social Awareness:** Campaigns like **"Stop Food Waste"** and initiatives by the **FSSAI** (Food Safety and Standards Authority of India) aim to sensitize citizens about the **environmental** and **economic** costs of food wastage.

questions.question: What does the term 'Blue Washing' refer to as per the News reports in 2025?

options.text: The practice of portraying polluting industries as environmentally-friendly
A new method for water purification
Cleaning rivers to make them blue

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The practice of portraying polluting industries as environmentally-friendly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bluewashing** is a deceptive marketing practice where companies overstate their commitment to **social responsibility** or **water sustainability** to distract from their actual impact. ***Hence, Option B is correct.***
 
• The term originates from the **blue color** of the **United Nations (UN) flag**, specifically referring to companies that join the **UN Global Compact** to use its reputation as a shield for poor practices.
 
• In recent **2024-2025 news reports**, the term has expanded to include **"Blue Economy"** claims, where industries like **deep-sea mining** or **industrial fishing** falsely portray themselves as ocean-friendly.
 
• The primary **feature** of **Bluewashing** is the use of humanitarian or **marine conservation** rhetoric to mask **labor violations**, **water pollution**, or lack of **ethical governance**.
 
• Unlike **Greenwashing**, which focuses on overall **climate** and **carbon emissions**, **Bluewashing** specifically targets **social justice** and **aquatic ecosystems**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The United Nations Global Compact**:

 
 
• Launched in the **year 2000**, it is the **world's largest voluntary corporate citizenship initiative**.
 
• It encourages businesses to adopt **ten principles** covering **human rights**, **labor standards**, and **anti-corruption**.
 
• **Bluewashing** occurs when a **member organization** signs these principles for **publicity** but fails to implement **substantive changes**.
 
 
 
• **Related Terminology**:
 
 
• **Greenwashing**: The practice of making **misleading claims** about the **environmental benefits** of a product, service, or technology.
 
• **Pinkwashing**: Using **LGBTQ+ rights** or **breast cancer awareness** branding to promote a company without meaningful **financial or systemic support**.
 
• **Social Washing**: A broader **category** where companies hide their **poor social records** behind **charitable donations** or **marketing campaigns**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Landscape in 2025**:
 
 
• Global bodies such as the **European Union** and the **US SEC** are implementing **stricter ESG disclosure norms** to curb **Bluewashing**.
 
• In **India**, the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** introduced the **Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR)** to ensure **transparency** in corporate claims.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of "Blue"**: The term "Blue" signifies two major pillars: the **United Nations Global Compact** (social) and **Sustainable Development Goal 14 (SDG 14)**, which focuses on **Life Below Water**.
 
• **Common Applications**: **Bluewashing** is frequently observed in the **shipping industry**, **textile manufacturing** (due to **water waste**), and **offshore oil drilling** companies.
 
• **Consequences**: Companies found guilty of **misleading consumers** face **legal penalties**, **loss of investor trust**, and significant **reputational damage**.
 
• **Distinction from Option A, C, and D**: **Bluewashing** is a **socio-economic concept** rather than a **chemical process** (Option A), a **purification method** (Option C), or a **physical cleaning task** (Option D). These options are **incorrect** as they interpret the term **literally** rather than in its **corporate ethics** context.

questions.question: Which Section of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, ensures that women are NOT excluded from Waqf property inheritance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Section 3A(2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Section 3A(2)** is a pivotal provision introduced in the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024** (referred to as the **2025 Act** contextually following its legislative timeline), which explicitly prohibits the creation of a **Waqf** that results in the denial of inheritance rights to legal heirs, specifically emphasizing that **women** must not be excluded.
 
• This section mandates that a person can only dedicate property to a **Waqf** if it does not infringe upon the **Succession Rights** of their family members. Under traditional practices, sometimes property was dedicated to **Waqf-alal-aulad** (Waqf for descendants) in a manner that bypassed female heirs; this amendment directly addresses such **Gender Discrimination**.
 
• The amendment clarifies that the **Right to Inheritance** is paramount, and any **Waqf** deed found to be depriving heirs of their rightful share, especially women who are often vulnerable in property disputes, will be considered **void** to that extent.
 
• This move is part of a broader reform to the **Waqf Act, 1995**, aimed at ensuring **Social Justice** and aligning religious property management with the **Constitutional Principles** of equality and non-discrimination.
 
• The provision ensures that the **legal heirs** under personal law retain their claims, preventing the misuse of **Waqf** as a tool to disinherit daughters or widows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Waqf:** A **Waqf** is the permanent dedication of movable or immovable property by a person professing **Islam** for any purpose recognized by Muslim Law as pious, religious, or charitable. The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, seeks to rename the original act to the **United Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act, 1995**.
 
• **Gender Representation in Boards:** Apart from inheritance rights, the new amendments mandate the inclusion of at least **two women** members in both the **Central Waqf Council** and the **State Waqf Boards**. This ensures that women have a direct say in the administration of **Waqf** properties.
 
• **Waqf-alal-aulad:** This specific type of **Waqf** is created for the maintenance and support of the donor's own family and descendants. The new **Section 3A(2)** ensures that this practice cannot be used to selectively provide for male descendants while excluding **female descendants**.
 
• **Inclusion of Non-Muslims:** The amendment bill also proposes that a person must have been practicing **Islam** for at least **five years** to create a **Waqf**, and it allows for **non-Muslim** representation in the administrative bodies to increase transparency and diversity.
 
• **Role of the Collector:** The bill proposes to give the **District Collector** the power to determine whether a property is **Waqf** property or **Government land**. This shifts some adjudicatory power away from **Waqf Tribunals** to the civil administration to resolve long-standing land disputes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Abolition of "Waqf by User":** The **2024/2025 Amendment** seeks to eliminate the concept of **Waqf by User**, where a property was deemed **Waqf** simply because it had been used for religious purposes for a long time. Now, a formal **Waqf-nama** (deed) and registration are mandatory.
 
• **Centralized Portal:** The government is introducing a **Centralized Registration Portal** for the **Registration of Waqf properties**, ensuring that all **Mutawallis** (managers) upload details of their assets to prevent **Encroachments** and illegal sales.
 
• **Tribunal Reforms:** While **Waqf Tribunals** previously had final authority, the new amendments propose that their decisions can be appealed in **High Courts** within a specific timeframe, usually **ninety days**, ensuring a check on judicial power within the **Waqf** framework.
 
• **Impact on Minority Rights:** Proponents of the bill argue it empowers **Muslim women** and **Pasmanda Muslims**, while critics argue it may interfere with **Article 26** of the **Constitution of India**, which grants religious denominations the right to manage their own affairs.

questions.question: What is the primary function of Rajasthan’s MadhuNetr DR‑AI system launched by the state health department in 2025?

options.text: A telemedicine platform for rural teleconsultations
A blockchain system for managing patient records
An AI tool for monitoring heart health remotely
An AI system for diabetic retinopathy screening

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An AI system for diabetic retinopathy screening**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **MadhuNetr DR‑AI system** is a specialized artificial intelligence software tool launched by the **Government of Rajasthan’s Medical and Health Department** in early **2025** to combat **blindness** caused by diabetes.
 
• Its primary function is the automated **screening of Diabetic Retinopathy (DR)**, a complication of **diabetes** that affects the **retina** of the eye. ***Hence, Option D is correct.***
 
• The system utilizes **Deep Learning algorithms** to analyze **fundus images** (back of the eye) captured by specialized cameras, identifying microaneurysms and hemorrhages that indicate early-stage damage.
 
• The deployment of this **AI technology** aims to provide mass screening in **District Hospitals** and **Community Health Centers (CHCs)** across **Rajasthan**, particularly in areas where **Ophthalmologists** are not readily available.
 
• By using **automated interpretation**, the system provides **real-time reports**, allowing for immediate referral to tertiary eye care centers for patients identified with "referable DR," thus preventing irreversible **vision loss**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Diabetic Retinopathy (DR):**

 
 
• It is a **microvascular complication** of **Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes**. High blood sugar levels damage the tiny blood vessels in the **retina**, leading to swelling, leaking, or the growth of abnormal new vessels.
 
• In **India**, nearly **1 in 5** people with **diabetes** may suffer from some form of **DR**, and it remains a leading cause of **preventable blindness** among the working-age population.
 
 
 
• **Role of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare:**
 
 
• **AI in diagnostics** helps in bridging the gap between high patient volumes and the shortage of medical specialists. In the context of **MadhuNetr**, the **AI engine** acts as a triage tool that can process thousands of images with **high sensitivity and specificity** (often exceeding **90%**).
 
• The use of **Cloud-based AI** allows health workers at the **village or block level** to upload images and receive instant feedback, a process known as **Point-of-Care (PoC) screening**.
 
 
 
• **Other Health Initiatives in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• **Rajasthan** has been a pioneer in health schemes such as the **Chiranjeevi Health Insurance Scheme** (now integrated with **Ayushman Bharat**) and the **Nirogi Rajasthan** campaign.
 
• The state health department also utilizes **e-Sanjeevani** for **telemedicine** and **tele-consultations**, which is different from the specific diagnostic focus of **MadhuNetr**. ***Hence, Option A is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Features:** The **MadhuNetr** system is designed to work with both **mydriatic** (dilated) and **non-mydriatic** (non-dilated) fundus cameras, making the screening process more comfortable for the **patient**.

• **Early Warning Systems:** NDMA works closely with the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** and the **Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)** to disseminate **real-time alerts** to the **population**.

questions.question: On 2 November 2025, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) deployed the advanced naval communication satellite GSAT‑7R (CMS-03) into orbit from which launch site?

options.text: Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station, Thumba

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** successfully deployed the **GSAT-7R** satellite, also known by its commercial designation **CMS-03**, on **2 November 2025**. This satellite is a dedicated **naval communication satellite** designed to provide a significant boost to the **Indian Navy**'s maritime communication capabilities.
 
• The launch was conducted from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)**, which is located in **Sriharikota**, **Andhra Pradesh**. This site serves as **India**'s primary spaceport due to its proximity to the equator and its location on the east coast, which provides a velocity boost for eastward launches over the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The **GSAT-7R** is a replacement for the aging **GSAT-7** satellite, which was launched in **2013**. It is equipped with advanced **UHF**, **S-band**, **C-band**, and **Ku-band** payloads to facilitate secure, real-time communication between **Indian Navy** warships, submarines, aircraft, and land-based command centers. ***Hence, the statement regarding Satish Dhawan Space Centre being the launch site is correct.***
 
• The satellite was launched using the **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV)** or **LVM3** (Launch Vehicle Mark 3), which is **ISRO**'s heaviest launch vehicle, capable of carrying large payloads into **Geostationary Transfer Orbit (GTO)**.
 
• The deployment of **CMS-03** ensures **maritime domain awareness** over the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**, supporting the **country**'s strategic interests and ensuring **national security**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), SHAR:** Established in **1971**, it is the sole satellite launch station of **India**. It is situated on the **Sriharikota** island in the **Nellore** district of **Andhra Pradesh**. It features **two** active launch pads that facilitate the launch of **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **LVM3** rockets.
 
• **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS):** Located in **Thiruvananthapuram**, **Kerala**, this station was established in **1963**. It is primarily used for launching **sounding rockets** for upper atmospheric research due to its proximity to the **magnetic equator**. It does not possess the infrastructure to launch heavy **communication satellites** like **GSAT-7R**.
 
• **UR Rao Satellite Centre (URSC):** Formerly known as the **ISRO Satellite Centre (ISAC)**, it is located in **Bengaluru**, **Karnataka**. This is the lead center for the **design**, **development**, and **construction** of all **Indian** satellites. While **GSAT-7R** was built here, it was transported to **Sriharikota** for the actual launch.
 
• **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC):** Situated in **Thiruvananthapuram**, **VSSC** is the main center for **design** and **development** of satellite launch vehicles (rockets). It is named after the father of the **Indian space program**, **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GSAT-7 Series (Rukmini):** The **GSAT-7** satellite was **India**'s first dedicated multi-band military satellite. It significantly improved the **Indian Navy**'s ability to operate far from the coastline by providing a footprint that covers the entire **Indian Ocean**.
 
• **CMS Nomenclature:** **ISRO** recently started using the **CMS** (Communication Satellite) prefix for its **communication satellites**. For instance, **CMS-01** was launched in **December 2020** to replace **GSAT-12**. **GSAT-7R** falling under the **CMS-03** designation follows this administrative **rebranding** strategy.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** The **GSAT-7R** (**CMS-03**) provides **network-centric warfare** capabilities, allowing for the seamless integration of various **naval assets**. It plays a vital role in the **Security and Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR)** initiative led by the **Government of India**.
 
• **Launch Date and Year:** The specific mission on **2 November 2025** represents **ISRO**'s continued commitment to indigenous satellite technology under the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** mission.

questions.question: In April 2025, under which campaign did the Reserve Bank of India launch its official WhatsApp channel to promote digital safety and literacy?

• The **Reserve Bank of India** (**RBI**) launched its official **WhatsApp** channel in **April 2025** as part of its flagship public awareness initiative, **RBI Kehta Hai**, to bolster **digital safety** and **financial literacy**.
 
• The primary objective of the **WhatsApp** channel is to provide **real-time** updates, safety tips, and information regarding **banking regulations** directly to the users' mobile phones, ensuring a wider reach across **urban** and **rural** India.
 
• The **RBI Kehta Hai** campaign is a **multi-media** and **multi-lingual** initiative, delivering messages in **14 Indian languages** to ensure that financial education is accessible to diverse linguistic groups.
 
• This digital expansion targets the prevention of **cyber-frauds**, such as **identity theft**, **vishing**, and **phishing**, by educating customers on the importance of never sharing their **OTP**, **PIN**, or **CVV** with anyone. ***Hence, the statement regarding the campaign name is correct.***
 
• By utilizing the **WhatsApp Business Platform**, the **RBI** aims to simplify complex financial concepts for **common citizens**, **senior citizens**, and **students**, making the central bank more accessible to the general public.

The **WhatsApp** channel often integrates information on how to reach the **Ombudsman** for grievance redressal.

• **Collaboration with NPCI:** The **Reserve Bank** works closely with the **National Payments Corporation of India** (**NPCI**) to secure **UPI** (**Unified Payments Interface**) transactions. **RBI** often uses its campaigns to highlight features like **UPI Lite** and **UPI 123Pay** for **feature phone** users.
 
• **Cyber Crime Helpline:** The campaign frequently promotes the **National Cyber Crime Helpline Number 1930** and the **Sanchar Saathi** portal, which are critical tools for reporting **financial frauds** within the "**Golden Hour**" to recover stolen funds.
